claims.text: 16th Street & Julian Avenue had 37 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 2 people killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $2.5 million a year.
No crash pattern here stands out against the city's worst crash locations.

This corner got continental crosswalks in 1899. Across the city: at 780 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (+4%, 95% interval -25% to +33%) could be zero. Repeating it here is not supported by the city's own record.
The city's painted safety zones: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (+2%, 95% interval -20% to +34%) could be zero); a second run of the same design on 780 sites agrees.
Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 2.0 crashes a year (CMF 4215, the median of 4 eligible records), worth $689,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.
Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 1.1 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites), worth $380,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.
The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA) is responsible for 16th Street, Valencia Street (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA) is ready to draft from these facts.
